findings.title: D7 (vi): the loop's goal test trusts a held state that no observation refreshes after the cargo move home
findings.problem: With goal_at_home on, _loop_done ends the episode when held_body_id equals the target body and the last move to q_home passed the at-home test. held_body_id is set by the pick's tactile check and cleared only on the place and stack paths (test_full_pipeline.py:2089, 2126, 2149, 2333, 2379, 2402 at 852b319). Nothing observes the grip after a move: detect_execution_collisions skips the held body and its result is unused, world_integrity_check leaves the held object out of its reconciliation (execution.py:1845, 1872) and register_new_detections skips it (test_full_pipeline.py:1277). Today the target is never moved after its verified pick, so the gap did not exist; D7 puts the long cargo move between the verified pick and the goal test. The loop can therefore declare K(holding target) reached on a literal that the pad contacts and the post-move render already contradict; Phase 6's _verify_holding then relabels the run physics_mismatch, and the dropped target is never re-registered or re-picked. The POD loop ends on a belief that ignores an available observation, against methods.tex:188 (replan whenever reality diverges from the plan's assumption).
findings.evidence: B3's own test (4) shows it (PAPER_AUDIT.txt at 8242937, lines 5699-5720): the corrective move to q_home passes the at-home test (9.8e-5 rad after an 8-step hold) while the cube 'rolled out of the pads during the corrective move (telemetry GRIP_LOST); the episode ended physics_mismatch', so the loop stopped on the stale flag and only Phase 6 noticed. BF#11 (i) (lines 5836-5845): the die-class box left the pads on the move home in 91 of 96 probe trials, so B7 will take this path on most episodes it reaches.
findings.suggested_fix: Make D7 (vi)'s 'target held' an observation, default off with the rest of D7, in the main pipeline under the B3 acceptance: after every move made while holding (at least the move to q_home, before at_home_ok can end the loop), apply the tactile rule the pipeline already uses (_assert_held_contact on held_body_id: both pads, squeeze at least 0.5 N); on a loss clear held_body_id and the cargo data, let the same post-move integrity render register the dropped body, and replan; bound the new cycle with the existing transit_loss_counts three-strike rule so R7 holds. Record it in D7 (vi) and its BF#.

findings.title: H3: D7 as the bridge runs it is a model tweak recorded without BEFORE / AFTER / CLAIM EFFECT lines
findings.problem: policy.py turns D7 on (goal_at_home, held_cargo_resolve, home_hold_step_cap 52). That changes the POD loop the thesis states: Algorithm 1 sets q to the home configuration (methods.tex:198), while D7 judges the initial readback and may name it q_readback_0 (BF#10 decision (2), taken beyond the plan text); Algorithm 1 updates q after each action (methods.tex:211), while D7 names the readback after a move to q_home by TAMPURA's tolerance test and otherwise by a fresh symbol; methods.tex:188 lists the loop's exits and D7 adds home_not_reached; the goal gains at_config(q_home); and the Boxel set gains the pseudo-boxel home, which names no volume and carries no Know-If literal for the target (methods.tex:84 calls the Boxels a partition of the workspace with one fluent per object and Boxel; under the domain's reading the target's presence in home stays unknown for good, harmless for planning because no sense or pick can ground on it). Each part is small and POD-expressible, but H3 asks for an entry with BEFORE / AFTER / CLAIM EFFECT lines: P4.5 M3 is one sentence covering only the goal form and the init facts; BF#10 books all of D7 as HONESTY CLASS refactor with CLAIM EFFECT 'none on the thesis scenes (every new behaviour is off)'; BF#12, which switches it on, records CLAIM EFFECT none, class translation; and the claim ledger's sentence on find_dice-only tweaks names M1, M2, M6 and M7, not M3. The claim effect of D7 as run in find_dice is recorded nowhere.
findings.evidence: M3 text at PAPER_AUDIT.txt:4296-4298; BF#10 decision (2) at 5677-5681 and its CLAIM EFFECT and HONESTY CLASS at 5722-5723; BF#12 at 5922-5923; methods.tex:84, 188, 194-221; test_full_pipeline.py:1236-1244, 1777-1829 and pddlstream_planner.py:903-915, 962-967 (852b319).
findings.suggested_fix: Give M3 its H3 lines. BEFORE: goal (holding T); q starts as q_home by assumption; a readback is named after the planned target whatever the residual; the exits of methods.tex:188. AFTER: the goal conjunct; the home pseudo-boxel (no volume, no Know-If literal, excluded from every enumeration, asserted); the initial readback judged by TAMPURA's test; tolerance-gated naming with q_readback_k; home_not_reached; the final hold; the cargo re-solve. CLAIM EFFECT: the paper says that in the find_dice runs lines 198, 199 and 211 of Algorithm 1, the exit list of methods.tex:188 and the partition sentence of methods.tex:84 carry these qualifications; none on the thesis scenes. Reclassify D7-on as model tweak M3 (in BF#10 or a new BF#), add M3 to the claim ledger's find_dice-only sentence, and list the naming rule beside 'at-home strictness' in P4.6.

findings.title: D7 (v): an at-home miss in mid-plan does not end the plan
findings.problem: After a move to q_home fails the test, current_config becomes q_readback_k, but the dispatcher breaks only at the second consecutive miss; the step closes with dispatch_end('ok') (:2509) and the plan goes on. A later step of the same plan that starts from q_home (a move(q_home, ...)) then runs with its precondition at_config(q_home) false in the belief, and its start-diff check (1e-2 rad) does not re-solve a small miss unless the hand holds something. D7 (v)'s 'the planner itself plans the corrective move' holds only when the move to q_home is the plan's last step. Rare, since a mid-plan visit to q_home costs extra moves, but it is a step executed past an observation that contradicted its precondition.
findings.evidence: Renaming at test_full_pipeline.py:1797-1801; break only on home_misses >= 2 at :1822-1829; no other exit before :2509 for a miss (852b319).
findings.suggested_fix: On a miss with steps left in the plan, end the plan with a labelled status (stale_precondition, or a new one added to run_logger.STEP_END_STATUSES and bridge_gates.G3_STATUSES) so the replan starts from q_readback_k; or assert and log that every move to q_home was the plan's last step.

findings.title: The run report prints a wall-clock exhaustion for the new home_not_reached exit
findings.problem: report_run_outcome has one branch per exit reason but none for home_not_reached, so an episode ended by D7 (vi)'s bound prints 'FAILED: Ran out of wall-clock budget after N plans with M unsearched shadows remaining'. The JSON exit_reason is right; the console line that the record and B7's watchers read names a different cause.
findings.evidence: No 'home_not_reached' in report_run_outcome's elif chain (run_logger.py:454-548 at 852b319); main() sets exit_reason = 'home_not_reached' at test_full_pipeline.py:1823.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a branch that names the bound (two consecutive planned moves to q_home left TAMPURA's test false) with the last max |dq| from the at_home_test ledger row.

findings.title: P4.6's disclosure list omits the belief-posed shadow cast and still carries the dropped 'cups partly out of frame' note
findings.problem: R6 says the bridge's plan-twin shadow cast 'is disclosed', but P4.6's table-note list has no entry for it. In the bridge every lateral shadow is cast against the plan twin posed from the belief at all three cast sites (generate_boxels through _ObjectBoxLookup, register_new_detections, the rediscovery path: boxel_env.py:1616-1617, execution.py:2401-2403, 3035-3036 at 852b319), registered bodies at their estimates and unregistered ones parked, while the thesis runs cast against the simulated world, where a ray can stop at an unregistered body (item (h)). The change keeps the model POD-consistent (a shadow becomes a function of the belief) and is stricter than the thesis pipeline, so it belongs in the notes. The same list still ends with 'every cup partly out of frame', which BF#11 (e) drops; and that drop rests on layout disclosures which BF#12 decision (4) says ran with NaN inertia on the b and e cups and are to be re-measured before B6.
findings.evidence: P4.6 list text at 4484-4499; R6 at 4596-4597 ('the bridge is stricter than the thesis pipeline here, which is disclosed'); BF#11 'is dropped' at 5806; BF#12 (4) at 5898-5904.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the shadow-cast difference to P4.6's notes; remove 'every cup partly out of frame' there or make it conditional; mark BF#11's drop provisional until the re-run with the corrected inertia confirms every cup's AABB in frame.

findings.title: M1's CLAIM EFFECT cites BF#2 for the necessity measurement that BF#11 (h) made
findings.problem: M1's CLAIM EFFECT says the clearance pose was 'measured necessary for this eye placement (BF#2)'. BF#2 is B0's gate record (BF#2 (h) moved B1's record to the next free number); the measurement is BF#11 (h). The adoption itself follows D5's pre-registered rule: bf/BF11_b1p2/probe_h.json gives worst blocked fraction 1.0 (a_cups_ud at (0.375, -0.105)) against the 0.05 threshold, and the 5 cm grid can only underestimate a maximum over every cell of W, so the verdict stands.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite BF#11 (h) in M1's CLAIM EFFECT.

findings.title: Holding model: plans certify moves with the cargo at the approach offset or none, the executor with the pick's offset; the pre-existing half is unrecorded
findings.problem: compute-kin gives every pick and place configuration grasp_ee_offset = grasp.position (0.10 or 0.06 m, the approach offsets), and plan_motion takes the held set and offset from the endpoints, so a planned move after a pick checks the cargo 6 to 10 cm below the EE, and a planned move to q_home checks no cargo (held set = intersection of the ignored sets, empty for q_home). The real cargo hangs 2 to 3 cm below the EE (_grasp_ee_to_obj_z, WP2b), which D7 (iv)'s readbacks and runtime re-solve use. Within one episode the planner's model of holding and the executor's therefore differ; the bridge relies on the runtime re-solve and a motion_resolve_failed replan to reconcile them, which is POD-acceptable as optimism but should be stated. The pre-existing half (the thesis runs certified every planned move while holding with the cargo 4 to 8 cm too low; the 2026-08-22 F10 fix calls 0.10 m 'the true carried height', superseded by WP2b) appears only as the rationale of BF#10 decision (3), not as a finding.
findings.evidence: streams.py:1469 'config.grasp_ee_offset = grasp.position'; :966 held set by intersection; robot_utils.py:385-388 cargo at ee_pos minus offset; execution.py:1299-1314 held_cargo_config; PAPER_AUDIT.txt:1356-1370 (F10) and 5682-5686 (BF#10 decision (3)) at 8242937.
findings.suggested_fix: File the planning-side cargo height as its own PAPER_AUDIT finding against the thesis pipeline (motion level; methods.tex:182-184 describe the collision checks), and add to D7 (iv)'s disclosure that plans still certify moves while holding with the approach-height cargo or none, the re-solve applying the pick's offset.

findings.title: Suspicion: YCB plan twins are posed by their centre of mass, not by the believed box
findings.problem: create_ycb shifts the geometry by minus the visual mesh's centre of mass, so a twin's base frame is that centre of mass; sync_to_plan_client poses the base, upright, at the registry box centre. For an inverted cup the centre of mass is not the box centre (the closed end is on top), so the twin cup that the shadow rays and the motion planner meet sits offset from the box the belief holds. G8(c) passes because it compares base positions only. The offset is not measured here, so this is a suspicion; for the primitives of our scenes the two centres coincide.
findings.evidence: Their create_ycb: geometry_pose = Pose(point=-mesh.center_mass) for both shapes; boxel_env.py:852-857 poses pid at bd.center with identity orientation; gate_hooks._check_twin compares getBasePositionAndOrientation with bd.center.
findings.suggested_fix: Measure the per-class offset once in the plan client (twin AABB centre minus base origin at identity orientation); compensate it when building the twin, or extend G8(c) to compare the twin's AABB centre with the registry centre within a stated tolerance.

findings.title: B3's acceptance failed by its own rule and Q13 is open, yet B2 and B1 part 2 were built on B3
findings.problem: The pre-registered acceptance fails on the plan-count clause (reproduced differences on seeds 100, 105 and 119; acceptance_report.json 'pass': false). BF#10 correctly stays OPEN and asks the user (Q13), whose alternative is to 'investigate further before B2 lands'; B2 (852b319, 8242937) then landed on 526b358 and BF#11 measured with it, which pre-empts that alternative without a recorded decision. On the substance, a reading of every default path of B3 finds no behaviour change on our scenes: the reach limits come from the same constants, the pick floor stays 35 mm through pick_contact_floor, readback configurations stay plain RobotConfig objects when held_cargo_resolve is off, at_home_ok and the at-home branch are inert when goal_at_home is off, compute-kin's early return fires only for the id 'home', the extra ignored self pair (8, 11) names a link without collision shape, and no new RNG draw is added. That supports Q13's proposed reading; the decision stays the user's.
findings.evidence: acceptance_report.json: reproduced_plan_count_diffs [100, 105, 119], reproduced_outcome_flips []; git log order 526b358, 8f122de, 96239d9, 852b319, 8242937.
findings.suggested_fix: Obtain the user's Q13 answer before gate 1 closes for B3, record that B2 and B1 part 2 ran on B3 while Q13 was open, and keep B3 off main-paper-icaps-2027 until then.
